title: Minimize Manhattan Distances
summary: Given an array of points with their 2D coordinates, where each point is represented as [xi, yi], find the minimum possible value for the maximum Manhattan distance between any two points after removing exactly one point from the array.
statement: Given an array of points with their 2D coordinates, where each point is represented as [xi, yi], find the minimum possible value for the maximum Manhattan distance between any two points after removing exactly one point from the array.
constraints: points contains at least three integer coordinate pairs.
Remove exactly one point, then measure the maximum Manhattan distance among every remaining pair.
Return the minimum possible maximum distance.
reference_solution:
def minimum_max_manhattan_after_removal(points):
    size=len(points);plus=sorted((x+y,index) for index,(x,y) in enumerate(points));minus=sorted((x-y,index) for index,(x,y) in enumerate(points))
    answer=10**30
    for removed in range(size):
        plus_low=plus[1][0] if plus[0][1]==removed else plus[0][0]
        plus_high=plus[-2][0] if plus[-1][1]==removed else plus[-1][0]
        minus_low=minus[1][0] if minus[0][1]==removed else minus[0][0]
        minus_high=minus[-2][0] if minus[-1][1]==removed else minus[-1][0]
        answer=min(answer,max(plus_high-plus_low,minus_high-minus_low))
    return answer

hints: Manhattan distance equals the maximum difference in the transformed coordinates x+y and x-y.
Sort both projections with point indices; after each removal select the first/last entry not carrying that index.
For every removed index compute both remaining projection ranges and minimize their maximum.
The projection identity gives the exact diameter, and only an endpoint can change when one indexed point is removed.
